title: Use first-party authorized Case Workspace handoff and revalidated return from native Case Queue browser
goal: Connect existing first-party server Workspace handoff and POST return to a bounded native browser interaction, preserving currently applied filters/page, checking the exact Case independently, retaining the transient token only in JS memory and obtaining a fresh authorized page before redisplaying data.
invariants: CAP-INV-101 Case Queue → Case Workspace Class-0 handoff uses ONLY existing first-party GET /case-queue?open_case and POST /case-queue/return with host-authenticated per-object Case/Incident/Finding and Saved View permissions.
Untrusted opaque return token exists ONLY in volatile JS memory; never URL, local/session storage, logs, cookies or persistent Case mutation.

Previously applied query, status/owner/freshness/sort, exact Case ID and page cursor are bound to opening and revalidating return; old Case data is cleared on navigation or failure; fresh GET needed before redisplay.
Full Case Workspace is NOT hosted here; this opt-in read-only context handoff cannot masquerade as actual Case Workspace, a Shared Inspector or grant of authorization.
security_properties: Server reauthorizes Case and nested sources for open and return independently, including page cursor and tenant/environment; client's old row is never authority.
Fail-closed mismatched Case ID or screen, malformed token, rejected POST, stale filtering or unauthorized cursor: no stale data rendered.
Only transient in-memory return token sent via same-origin no-store POST JSON body; never a query parameter. Host remains responsible for cookie CSRF, IAM, audit and TLS.

migration.rationale: Opt-in same-origin host-mounted static browser with no changed persistence or Case schema

rollback.strategy: Disable opt-in workspace handoff buttons and retain previous browser GET filter/list/Inspector; backend first-party J/K/N unchanged
verification: Existing native authorized Queue and Inspector flows remain available
No return token or Case data persisted

inputs: CAP-INV-101 §17/25 Case Queue → Case Workspace → exact filtered Queue return is not yet linked from native browser, while existing backend E10-INV-101J/K/N already authorizes handoff and return.

Existing E10-INV-101S browser applied snapshot q/status/owner/freshness/sort and cursor-bound Case page with independently reauthorized Inspector on frozen PR #150 exact SHA a5034c3dfb6ae23a9fa61725e7d9057277db72fe.
outputs: Native read-only Open workspace handoff control calling existing server GET open_case with exactly current applied filtered page, and bounded explicit transient context view.
Return control using existing POST return_token, client assertion of matching expected Case/projection and fresh server-authorized Queue GET before returning to the visible page.
Clear volatile state on denied/mismatched/stale requests, filter changes, pagination and pagehide; no new owner or data store.
acceptance_tests: Node DOM test executes actual browser.js: exact Case handoff request, volatile token NOT in URL, POST /case-queue/return JSON-only, fresh GET and original scroll restoration.
Node DOM test checks denial/mismatched Case/changed return projection wipes all sensitive Case rows without partial output.

Existing Node browser filtering, pagination and Inspector security tests remain green on exact-head engineering-kernel CHK-CASE-QUEUE-CONTRACT and CHK-SECURITY-TESTS unchanged >=90%; host Go HTTP/J/K/N tests retained.
Any production Case Workspace UI or Shared Inspector remains explicitly NOT implemented or accepted.

performance_budget.rationale: One existing authenticated GET handoff, one POST return reauthorization and one independent fresh Queue GET, no polling/extra runtime/index.
metrics: One first-party POST and one new authorized Queue GET per return

definition_of_ready: E10-INV-101S IMPLEMENTED on PR #150 exact HEAD a5034c3dfb6ae23a9fa61725e7d9057277db72fe with engineering-kernel 39320552192 SUCCESS; J/K/N existing first-party server handoff/return contracts already tested.
Bounded adapter confined to native browser one read-only context and transient state; host-side authentication/CSRF and full Workspace UI remain separately owned.
definition_of_done: Commit coherent native browser handoff/return UI and behavior tests, publish manifest and handoff with exact CI/evidence on child draft PR.
One independent read-only L2 for meaningful browser↔Workspace return security integration if stable; no full product acceptance or merge claim.
